articles.summary: India will look to seal the five-match T20I series when they face the West Indies in the fourth match at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in
articles.body: India will look to seal the five-match T20I series when they face the West Indies in the fourth match at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad on Wednesday. With India leading the series 2-1, the possibility of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi getting a chance has once again become a major talking point.India will aim to continue their winning run and put pressure on the visitors. The West Indies, meanwhile, will look to bounce back and keep the series alive.Ahead of the fourth T20I, Sooryavanshi shared a couple of pictures from his batting practice session."Stay seated," Sooryavanshi captioned the two-word post with a tornado and an hourglass emojis.India will look to take an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series. Captain Shreyas Iyer and coach Gautam Gambhir may prefer to stick with the same playing XI, including the opening pair of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson.However, former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar has backed teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, saying that the 15-year-old should play in India's Playing XI for the fifth T20I against the West Indies.India, led by Shreyas Iyer, currently lead the five-match series 2-1 and need just one more win to seal it. They started with a convincing eight-wicket victory but suffered a six-wicket defeat in the high-scoring second T20I. India bounced back with a 14-run win in the third match.Nayar wants Sooryavanshi to play the final T20ISpeaking ahead of the fourth T20I, Nayar said India should first focus on winning the series. A victory would allow the team management to give Sooryavanshi an opportunity in the final match.The young opener has not played in the series so far, with India continuing to back Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson at the top of the order."I would want India to go 3-1 up, and for the last game, Sooryavanshi plays. So keep it simple: Go 3-1 up, wrap the series up, and let Sooryavanshi play the last one," said Nayar on Star Sports.Hyderabad pitch expected to favour battersHyderabad is known for its batting-friendly conditions and short boundaries. Both teams could be involved in another high-scoring contest.The venue has witnessed successful T20I chases of 208 and 187. India have also come close to the 300-run mark here, recording the second-highest T20I total in matches between ICC Full Member countries.Hyderabad is also home to Sunrisers Hyderabad, one of the most aggressive batting teams in the Indian Premier League (IPL). Abhishek Sharma, Travis Head and Heinrich Klaasen have been key examples of the franchise's attacking approach.The venue has also witnessed huge totals in domestic and franchise cricket over the past two years, with scores of 310, 297, 286 and 277 being recorded.The pitch has recently been relaid, but conditions are still expected to favour batters. Dew could make batting easier in the second innings. With no rain predicted, the match is expected to take place without interruption.India vs West Indies 4th T20I: SquadsIndia: Shreyas Iyer (c), Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan (wk), Sanju Samson (wk), Tilak Varma (vc), Shivam Dube, Kuldeep Yadav, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav.West Indies: Shai Hope (c), Jewel Andrew, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Shimron Hetmyer, Akeal Hosein, Shamar Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul, Kamil Pooran, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Quentin Sampson, Romario Shepherd, Shamar Springer.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia vs South Africa: What England learned from first Test in Durban as Matt Renshaw inspires Australia win
articles.summary: Matt Renshaw nails down middle-order spot for Australia as questions remain over Marnus Labuschagne place in the side; And what about rusty-looking South Africa's struggles?' Watch the second Test in Gqeberha, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8am, Sunday (first ball 9am)
articles.body:
England won't get benefit of rusty-looking Proteas

It's nearly a year since the Proteas last played Test cricket - an impressive 2-0 series win in India - while this represented their first home Test since winning the World Test Championship final against Australia at Lord's in June 2025.

They looked short of a gallop, as a result.

There were encouraging contributions from Aiden Markram - in particular his 237-ball, near six-hour stay at the crease in the second innings in South Africa's ultimately futile attempt to bat out for a draw - and David Bedingham, who did well with a couple of 40s at No 3.

But they weren't telling enough totals for the longer format, with South Africa guilty of throwing away numerous starts in the first innings - six players scoring at least 30 but failing to kick on - as they surrendered a 106-run deficit.

There were a couple of failures from Ryan Rickelton at the top of the order, while the captain's contribution will also be questioned as Temba Bavuma managed just four runs total across his two innings.

The question is whether this was a sign of deeper problems for the side or simply the inevitable consequence of a rusty return to Test cricket after their extended absence.

England should have their answer by the time they arrive in South Africa ahead of their first Test in Johannesburg on December 17, as the hosts have two further Tests against Australia, followed by a two-match series against Bangladesh in November to get sufficiently up to speed.

Has Renshaw solved Australia's middle-order issues?

With his first-innings, career-best 190, Matt Renshaw might just have cemented himself a middle-order spot for Australia for the foreseeable future.

The player of the match - who also chipped in with 82 in the second innings and a couple of wickets with his part-time off-spin - helped rescue Australia from 124-6 on day one when in danger of surrendering control of the contest amid familiar top-order batting failings.

Instead, Australia posted a score of 390 deep into day two and never looked back from there.

If Renshaw has indeed grabbed hold of the No 5 position, at least for the rest of the series, there are still questions to be resolved regarding the makeup of the rest of the batting line-up.

Travis Head, for example, had previously made that position his own before being bumped up to open midway through the Ashes last winter. It was a move that paid dividends at the time, as he hit three hundreds in winning causes at Perth, Adelaide and Sydney. However, he has not passed 22 in his three Test appearances since, including falling foul of a couple of soft dismissals in Durban.

Renshaw has also opened previously for Australia, so might there be a switch of the two at some point? One to revisit prior to their trip to England next summer, perhaps?

For now though, Renshaw will surely get the benefit of a run in the middle order and Australia have bigger batting issues to resolve before determining how to best use Head.

Questions remain over Labuschagne and top order

Marnus Labuschagne's wait for a 12th Test ton lives on, stretching back to July 2023.

A hundred in the warm-up match prior to the series promised much, as did his pair of 37s in this Test before failing to convert either into a score of note - let alone a century.

Averaging only 25.29 with the bat in his 24 Tests played since last topping three figures at Old Trafford in the 2023 Ashes, Labuschagne was considered incrediblly fortunate to keep his place in this Australian side but it came as a result of a lack of alternative options staking a claim.

Maddinson last played Test cricket for Australia in late 2016, averaging 6.75 across his three appearances, with his career since stalled by injury, mental health issues, and then a testicular cancer diagnosis that sidelined him for most of last year.

As a result, the 34-year-old hadn't played a first-class match since March 2025 before returning to the Test team in Durban after injuries to other batting options Cameron Green and Josh Inglis.

His first-innings 33-ball duck was an inauspicious start to his second coming in international cricket, and though he played with a great deal more freedom in the second innings, with Australia well ahead of the game by that stage - striking six fours and a couple of sixes in his 48 off 38 balls - his place in the team will continue to come under scrutiny.

Especially as Green and Inglis are now set to be back available for the second Test in Gqeberha.

To jettison Maddison after only one game back would be incredibly harsh, but Australia will be eager to get golden-boy Green, in particular, back into the team - and Renshaw has blocked his most obvious route for return at No 5.

Could he come in for Labuschagne at No 3, or Beau Webster at No 7 after he was underused as an all-rounder here? There's still much to be resolved with the look of this batting line-up.

Hazlewood and co prove they're still a force

If there was one aspect of Australia's performance that should concern England, however, it's the continued quality and depth of their bowling attack.

Josh Hazlewood's career-best Test figures of 6-49 in the second innings completed a dominant performance by the visiting seamers. Skipper Pat Cummins had led the attack first time around, taking 3-54 to help dismiss South Africa for a below-par 284 on a decent batting deck.

The evergreen talents of 38-year-old off-spinner Nathan Lyon add a further dimension, while Australia also boast Scott Boland and Michael Neser in reserve.

That depth will matter over the coming months. Australia's attack is an ageing group, and the demands of an intense Test schedule - a four-match series at home to New Zealand and five away in India - following the trip to South Africa will test their fitness and durability.

How will they be holding up by the time the Ashes comes around on June 18 with the first Test at Trent Bridge?

For the time being though, any optimistic talk of Australia's attack being past their best by then looks massively premature.

South Africa team selection a head-scratcher

South Africa's team selection for the series opener raised some questions, particularly the decision to field two specialist spinners in Durban.

Keshav Maharaj and Simon Harmer offered a left and right-arm option, but neither proved particularly potent, with just the four wickets shared between them - including only one in the first innings, to Harmer's name, allowing Australia to recover from 124-6 to post 390.

The absence of Kagiso Rabada, having failed to recover from a hamstring injury in time for this Test, perhaps forced the selectors' hand, but it left their attack looking a little lopsided and somewhat patched together.

Wiaan Mulder, for example, should not be operating with the new ball in Test cricket.

The batting all-rounder took two wickets with it on the first morning, and burgled a couple more into day two, but was pretty ineffective otherwise for his 31 overs of hard toil through the Test.

The return of Anrich Nortje was encouraging. After an extended absence from Test cricket, the fast bowler showed glimpses of the pace and aggression that made him a major asset during his first stint in the side from 2019 to 2023.

And assuming Rabada is back fit and available for the second Test in Gqeberha, his return would provide greater balance and potency to South Africa's attack.

The prospect of Rabada, Nortje and the left-arm option of Marco Jansen steaming in would represent a much sterner challenge for Australia, and England in a couple months' time.

articles.title: Drama! Qais Ahmed's injury moment brings back memories of Gulbadin Naib's T20 World Cup incident
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Qais Ahmed grabbed attention in the closing stages of the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Qais Ahmed grabbed attention in the closing stages of the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi. The Afghanistan batter's injury moment reminded fans of Gulbadin Naib's incident during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Afghanistan put up a determined batting effort to secure a draw at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium. The hosts batted for 142 overs to avoid defeat against their Asian rivals.Qais played an important role in ensuring that the efforts of Afghanistan's batters, especially Sediqullah Atal, did not go in vain. Batting at number nine, he remained unbeaten on 49 off 80 balls and helped his team survive the final stages of the match.Qais Ahmed's injury moment in the final oversWith just 10 minutes left in the match, Qais blocked a delivery from Taijul Islam in the third-last over before going down while holding his left hamstring.The moment caught the attention of social media users, while Bangladesh players appeared pleased with the situation.The incident reminded fans of Naib's injury moment against Bangladesh during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Afghanistan won that match to reach the semi-finals of an ICC tournament for the first time.Qais made another important contribution in the final over, hitting two sixes as Afghanistan and Bangladesh settled for a draw.Sediqullah Atal scores maiden Test centuryAtal played a key role in Afghanistan's effort to save the Test. He scored 111 off 333 balls to register the first Test century of his career. He also became the first Afghanistan batter to score a century in the fourth innings of a Test match.Captain Rahmat Shah also had a memorable game. In his first Test as captain, he scored 105 in the first innings and followed it up with 51 in the second. Rahmat became only the sixth male cricketer to score a century and a half-century on his Test captaincy debut.Gulbadin Naib's injury incident at T20 World Cup 2024Afghanistan created history at the 2024 T20 World Cup by beating Bangladesh to reach the semi-finals of an ICC tournament for the first time. However, the match also drew attention because of an incident involving Naib.During the 12th over of Bangladesh's innings, Naib went down holding his hamstring shortly after head coach Jonathan Trott was seen signalling to the players to slow the game down. At that stage, Afghanistan were two runs ahead under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method, with the match finely balanced.Naib's injury led to the physios coming onto the field. Play was then stopped as rain interrupted the match. When the teams returned after a short break, Naib appeared to be moving comfortably. This led to criticism from some fans and experts, who questioned the timing of the incident and suggested it may have helped Afghanistan.Afghanistan eventually defeated Najmul Hossain Shanto's Bangladesh by eight runs under the DLS method. articles.summary: JAIPUR: Left-arm spinner Ajay Singh Kukna bagged a five-wicket haul to help Rajasthan take a crucial 89-run first innings lead against Tamil Nadu on the
articles.body: JAIPUR: Left-arm spinner Ajay Singh Kukna bagged a five-wicket haul to help Rajasthan take a crucial 89-run first innings lead against Tamil Nadu on the penultimate day of the Ranji Trophy match at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium here on Tuesday. Rajasthan ended the eventful Day 3 at 81-4 with an overall lead of 170.Vice-captain Mahipal Lomror (25 batting) and Kartik Sharma (30 batting) were holding fort with an unbeaten fifth-wicket stand of 50 runs after the hosts were tottering at 31/4.Unless a dramatic batting collapse happens on Wednesday morning, it will be a herculean task for the Sai Kishore-led team to pull off a victory from the Elite Group D opening encounter.A disciplined bowling effort backed by some excellent fielding from Rajasthan brought them back in the match. A slice of luck also helped them and put the rivals on the backfoot.Adopting a cautious approach, TN resumed at their overnight score of 167/4 with C Andre Siddharth and Sonu Yadav. Eying a first-innings lead on a flat track, both the batters didn’t take any risk and slowly built the innings. After adding just 36 runs in 24.5 overs, a terrible mix-up between them gifted the hosts the wicket of Yadav.Siddharh tried to repair the damage with Washington Sundar as they put on 61 runs for the sixth wicket.But Kukna turned things around with a gem of a delivery that uprooted the stumps of Siddharth (81). From 264/5, TN lost the rest of the wickets for 10 runs in a span of 4.2 overs in an extraordinary batting collapse.The 29-year-old Kukna (5-51) ended with his seventh five-wicket haul, while left-arm pacer Akash Singh was finally rewarded for his lion-hearted effort with a couple.TN tried to put up a fight with the ball as Sai Kishore picked up two quick wickets with the new ball in Rajasthan’s second innings. Pacers Saravana Kumar and Sonu Yadav took a wicket each and there were hopes of a comeback.However, Kartik-Lomror pair’s gutsy batting at the fag end of the day denied TN any further success.“It was a special effort. I am happy to strike at the crucial juncture to help my team gain a vital lead. We didn’t leak many runs when we were not getting wickets earlier in the day and that ultimately helped us. Manav and I both come from the same place (Sriganganagar) and we always enjoy bowling in tandem. We are in a good position now and can try for an outright win tomorrow,” Kukna told TOI after the day’s play.BRIEF SCORESRajasthan 363 and 81/4 in 34 overs (Kartik Sharma 30 batting, Mahipal Lomror 25 batting, Karan Lamba 13, Rohan Rajbhar 10; Sai Kishore 2-25, Saravana Kumar 1-4, Sonu Yadav 1-16) vs Tamil Nadu 274 in 98.4 overs (C Andre Siddarth 81, Pradosh Ranjan Paul 58, Narayan Jagadeesan 55, Washington Sundar 26, Baba Indrajith 26; Ajay Singh Kukna 5-51, Akash Singh 2-74).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Top-order batter Kevin Wickham has received his first call-up to the West Indies Test team for the upcoming two-match series in Bangladesh. The 15-member squad will play its final series of the 2025-2027 ICC World Test Championship cycle.The first Test will begin on October 28 in Mirpur, while the second match will start on November 5 in Sylhet.White-ball captain Shai Hope has been rested for the series after playing across all three formats for an extended period. He is currently leading the West Indies in their white-ball series against India.Wickham rewarded for strong domestic performancesThe 23-year-old Wickham has earned his maiden senior-level Test call-up after an impressive run in the West Indies Championship.He scored three consecutive centuries in the competition, with his highest score being 153. Wickham has now hit six centuries in 25 first-class matches at an average of over 40.Alzarri Joseph ruled out, Keemo Paul replaces himFast bowler Alzarri Joseph has been withdrawn from the squad led by Roston Chase following a routine medical assessment and consultation with specialists.Cricket West Indies (CWI) has decided to manage Joseph's workload to reduce the risk of injury because of the increased physical demands of red-ball cricket.Joseph will continue to work with the CWI medical team and specialists as he prepares to return to the longer format.All-rounder Keemo Paul has been named as Joseph's replacement for the Bangladesh series.John Campbell returns to the squadOpener John Campbell is back in the squad after recovering from a hamstring injury. The injury had ruled him out of the home series against Pakistan.The rest of the squad remains the same as the group that beat Sri Lanka and drew its series against Pakistan during the summer.Hope has been rested as the West Indies manage his workload ahead of the ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifier, scheduled for February next year.Daren Sammy sets sights on WTC rankingsWest Indies head coach Daren Sammy said the team wants to improve its position in the World Test Championship standings by winning the Bangladesh series."At the start of this World Test Championship cycle we set ourselves goals, and one of them was to finish in the top half of the rankings."Winning this series would move us closer to it. articles.body: India’s Test cricketers returned to domestic action in the opening round of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season after the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) asked available players to feature for their state teams.With India preparing for a two-Test tour of New Zealand, the matches offered players an opportunity to build form, but the results were mixed.While KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan and Sarfaraz Khan struggled with the bat, Ravindra Jadeja delivered an impressive all-round performance for Saurashtra.Mohammed Siraj and Washington Sundar also contributed to their teams’ campaigns.Jadeja shines as several batters struggleKL Rahul: Playing for Karnataka against Andhra Pradesh in Vijayawada, India’s Test vice-captain scored four runs in the first innings and one in the second.Yashasvi Jaiswal: The Mumbai opener was dismissed for a duck off 13 balls by Jagjit Singh against Chandigarh. articles.title: 'We immediately think of Chris Gayle': Cheteshwar Pujara's big statement on Abhishek Sharma
articles.summary: When Abhishek Sharma gets going, bowlers often find it difficult to stop him.
articles.body: When Abhishek Sharma gets going, bowlers often find it difficult to stop him. The left-handed batter is known for his big sixes, aggressive start and ability to change a match within a few overs. Abhishek once again showed his hitting ability in the third T20I against the West Indies. He smashed 69 off just 30 balls to help India register a 14-run victory and take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.His innings included six fours and five sixes. He reached his half-century in just 18 balls, registering his 14th T20I fifty.The performance earned praise from former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara, who compared Abhishek's ability in the shortest format to that of West Indies great Chris Gayle.Pujara compares Abhishek Sharma with Chris GaylePujara believes Abhishek has already established himself as one of India's best T20 players. He also said the young batter's name would be remembered for a long time.“Nobody thought that he would cross such a big milestone so quickly. But the way Abhishek has performed, I think he is probably one of the best T20 players the Indian team has had so far,” said Pujara on JioStar.Pujara then compared Abhishek with Gayle, who was known for his explosive batting in T20 cricket. He also praised Abhishek for showing greater maturity and understanding when to attack.“His name will be remembered for a long time. When we talk about the T20 format, we immediately think of Chris Gayle from the West Indies. Abhishek has that kind of ability. The way he showed maturity, especially in Indore, by taking a little time, even though five-six balls is a lot of time for him, shows that he is understanding his game a little better, recognising the opposition’s strengths, and batting accordingly. Now, in Hyderabad, he has played a lot on that ground, and that experience and familiarity matter, even in T20s,” Pujara said.Abhishek crosses 2,000 T20I runsThe third T20I against the West Indies was another milestone match for Abhishek. He became the sixth Indian men's cricketer to score 2,000 runs in T20 internationals. He also became the fastest batter in men's cricket to reach the milestone in terms of balls faced.At Holkar Stadium in Indore, Abhishek scored his 69 runs off 30 balls at a strike rate of 230. His aggressive start helped India post 223 runs, even though the team lost some momentum after his partnership with Ishan Kishan.The West Indies managed 209/7 in reply, giving India a 14-run victory. The win put India ahead 2-1 in the series. He has made 921 runs in 32 matches and innings at an average of 29.70 and a strike rate of 206.50. His tally includes one century and eight half-centuries. His score of 108 is the fastest T20I century by a batter from a Test-playing nation.Abhishek has also hit 68 sixes in T20Is this year, putting him level with India's T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav for the most sixes in a calendar year.However, Abhishek has hit a six every 6.55 balls, compared to Suryakumar's one every 9.13 balls.It was the seventh time he had scored a fifty within the first six overs of a T20I. articles.title: Gautam Gambhir turns 45: 'A fighter on the field' - special birthday wishes pour in
articles.summary: Former India cricketers Yuvraj Singh and Suresh Raina extended their birthday wishes to India head coach Gautam Gambhir as he turned 45 on Wednesday.
articles.body: Former India cricketers Yuvraj Singh and Suresh Raina extended their birthday wishes to India head coach Gautam Gambhir as he turned 45 on Wednesday. Both former teammates praised Gambhir, with Yuvraj promising his continued support and Raina highlighting his fighting spirit and contribution to Indian cricket.Yuvraj took to Instagram to wish Gambhir, expressing his support and hoping that the former India opener continues to achieve greater success."GG, you know I've always got your back and wish you only go from strength to strength! Happy birthday, brother. Always upwards, and keep making us proud! Lots of love," Yuvraj wrote.Raina also shared a birthday message for Gambhir on X, praising his attitude on the field and his commitment to Indian cricket."A fighter on the field, a champion at heart, and a man who has always stood tall for Indian cricket," Raina wrote."Wishing you good health, happiness, and many more milestones in your journey. Keep inspiring, keep leading," he added.Rohan Jaitley, Rajeev Shukla wish GambhirDelhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA) president Rohan Jaitley also wished Gambhir on his 45th birthday, saying Delhi was proud of his contribution to Indian cricket.“Happy Birthday, Gautam Gambhir! Wishing you good health, happiness and continued success. Delhi is proud of its own son and his invaluable contribution to Indian cricket. May you continue to inspire generations and take Indian cricket to greater heights,” Jaitley told IANS.BCCI vice president Rajeev Shukla also congratulated the India head coach, praising his passion and commitment to the sport.“Your passion for cricket, competitive spirit and unwavering commitment to Indian cricket continue to inspire. May you be blessed with good health, happiness and continued success as you contribute to the growth and glory of Indian cricket. Wishing you a wonderful year ahead,” Shukla wrote.Gambhir's journey from India opener to head coachGambhir was one of India's leading opening batters between 2003 and 2016 and formed a formidable partnership with Virender Sehwag. He played a crucial role in India's 2011 ODI World Cup triumph, scoring 393 runs in nine innings, including four half-centuries. His 97-run knock in the final against Sri Lanka at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium helped India chase down a target of 275 and win the trophy after 28 years.Across international cricket, Gambhir scored 10,324 runs in 242 matches at an average of 38.95, including 20 centuries and 63 half-centuries.He also enjoyed success in the Indian Premier League (IPL), leading Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) to titles in 2012 and 2014. As a batter, he scored 4,217 runs in 154 IPL matches, including 36 half-centuries.Gambhir took charge as India's head coach in July 2024. Under his leadership, India won the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy, the 2025 ACC Men's Asia Cup and the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer has climbed three places to a career-best fourth in the latest ICC T20 International rankings for batters after his strong start to the ongoing five-match home series against the West Indies.Iyer scored his maiden T20I century in the series opener in Lucknow. His rise to fourth place means India now have three players among the top four, with Ishan Kishan at the top and Abhishek Sharma in second place. Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan sits between them in third after reaching a career-best rating following his performances against Sri Lanka, the ICC said in a press release.Among other batters, Sri Lanka's Kusal Mendis moved up three places to 23rd, while West Indies' Sherfane Rutherford climbed 13 spots to joint 24th. India's Sanju Samson rose four places to joint 27th.Pakistan youngster Maaz Sadaqat made a significant jump, moving from outside the top 100 to 45th after his performances in the three-match series against Sri Lanka.West Indies all-rounder Roston Chase also made progress in the T20I rankings. He climbed 24 places to 23rd among bowlers and moved up two spots to third among all-rounders following his performances against India.Pakistan's Salman Mirza rose nine places to 14th in the T20I bowling rankings, while Saim Ayub gained eight spots to reach 54th.In the Test rankings, India's Ravindra Jadeja continued to hold a clear lead among all-rounders. South Africa's Wiaan Mulder moved up one place to fourth, while Simon Harmer climbed five spots to joint 23rd after their performances against Australia.Australia's 214-run win over South Africa in the first Test at Kingsmead in Durban also led to gains for several players in the latest ICC Test rankings. articles.title: 'He can be a great opener': Pat Cummins hints at batting reshuffle despite Matthew Renshaw's 272-run haul
articles.summary: Matthew Renshaw made a strong case for himself in Australia's first Test against South Africa in Durban, scoring 190 runs in the first innings and 82 in
articles.body: Matthew Renshaw made a strong case for himself in Australia's first Test against South Africa in Durban, scoring 190 runs in the first innings and 82 in the second to help his side secure a convincing victory. However, Australia captain Pat Cummins has indicated that the team could still shuffle its batting order for the second Test, depending on the conditions.Australia clinched a 214-run victory on Day 5 of the opening Test, with Josh Hazlewood producing a career-best performance of six wickets in the second innings. While Renshaw's impressive returns have strengthened his claim for a middle-order spot, Cummins remains open to different combinations as Australia prepare for the next encounter in Gqeberha.Cummins acknowledges Renshaw's impressive performanceCummins admitted that Renshaw's outstanding performance would make it difficult for the team management to justify moving him down the order. However, he stressed that the team would assess the conditions before finalising its batting combination."Give us a few days, we'll look at the conditions of the next Test. I mean, it's got to be pretty compelling to move Renshaw from there," Cummins said.The Australian captain also highlighted the possibility of using Travis Head at No. 5, adding that the team was evaluating how its top six batters, along with wicketkeeper Alex Carey, could function most effectively."So, if anything, I still think he [Renshaw] can be a great opener, and now he's got another string to his bow that he's found this week," Cummins added.Cameron Green's availability could influence Australia's plansRenshaw's promotion to the middle order came after Cameron Green suffered an abdominal injury, forcing Australia to reconsider its batting combination. The left-hander capitalised on the opportunity, scoring 190 in the first innings and following it up with 82 in the second to help Australia recover from a precarious position of 124/6 on the opening day.Australia's decision to recall Nic Maddinson and deploy him as an opener, nearly a decade after his previous Test appearance, also reflected the team's willingness to experiment with its batting order. Renshaw's recent success in the middle order in one-day cricket had influenced the decision to give him a different role.Australia keen to retain batting flexibilityCummins explained that Australia were confident about Marnus Labuschagne batting at No. 3 and Steve Smith at No. 4, while the positions at Nos. 6 and 7 also appeared settled. However, Maddinson's inclusion has provided the team with greater flexibility at the top of the order."We're pretty certain that we like Marn [Labuschagne] at No. 3, Smithy at No. 4, and then, the six and seven felt pretty locked up. I think bringing in Maddo, we really like the idea of bringing that flexibility," Cummins said.He added that the additional options could allow Australia to use Head, Renshaw or Maddinson at No. 5, depending on the team's requirements."We're very big on that flexibility. I know you're probably sick of us talking about it but, why not next week, have different openers if the conditions take us somewhere different, or swapping out the batting orders between innings," Cummins said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ajinkya Rahane, Ganguly play tennis-ball cricket with Britain's Prince WIlliam outside Buckingham Palace
articles.summary: Britain's Prince William turned The Mall, the famous London road leading to Buckingham Palace, into a temporary cricket pitch on Tuesday.
articles.body: Britain's Prince William turned The Mall, the famous London road leading to Buckingham Palace, into a temporary cricket pitch on Tuesday. He invited several current and former international cricketers for an informal game in the build up to an award by the British Royal.Former India captain Sourav Ganguly and Ajinkya Rahane, who recently retired from all forms of cricket, were among those who joined West Indies great Brian Lara and England players Joe Root and Harry Brook for the event.The Mall, a wide red-paved road in the heart of London, is usually the setting for royal processions and public celebrations. On Tuesday, however, it hosted a game of tennis-ball cricket as William picked up a bat and faced deliveries from Ganguly.Dressed in a shirt and sweater, the prince played a few shots and posed for selfies with onlookers. Ganguly gave a brief assessment of his batting."He batted alright," said Ganguly when asked for his verdict on the prince's skills.Rahane shared his experience in a LinkedIn post on Wednesday, describing the opportunity to play cricket on The Mall with Buckingham Palace in the background as a memorable one."Cricket has taken me to some remarkable venues across the world, but playing tennis-ball cricket right on The Mall in London with Buckingham Palace in the backdrop is an experience that will stay with me for a long time," Rahane said in a LinkedIn post on Wednesday."It was a privilege to spend time with HRH Prince William and catch up with wonderful friends and icons of the sport Dada, Brian Lara, Joe Root, Harry Brook, and everyone else who brought so much joy to the pitch."We spoke about the unifying spirit of cricket, our memories of playing in England and back home in India, and the responsibility we share toward the future.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Shami and co. help Bengal crush Delhi by nine wickets; Desai spins Gujarat to bonus-point win
articles.summary: Bengal began their Ranji Trophy Group C campaign with a nine-wicket win over Delhi after bowling out the visitors for 277 in their second innings and
articles.body: Bengal began their Ranji Trophy Group C campaign with a nine-wicket win over Delhi after bowling out the visitors for 277 in their second innings and chasing a target of 89 on the fourth and final day on Wednesday.Delhi resumed the day at 101 for three but were dismissed for 277 in 106.2 overs. Captain Ayush Badoni led the batting with 85 off 134 balls, hitting 10 fours, while wicketkeeper-batter Anuj Rawat scored 39 off 76 deliveries.Bengal had taken a first-innings lead after scoring 429 in reply to Delhi's 240. They needed only 15.3 overs to complete the chase, reaching 89 for one and securing the victory.Delhi had lost three wickets for 59 before Badoni and Rawat joined forces to steady the innings. Rawat was dismissed for 39 by Aamir Gani, while Yash Dhull made 22 before falling to Sumanta Gupta.Badoni continued to hold the innings together, but his dismissal for 85, caught by Abhimanyu Easwaran off Pradipta Pramanik, left Delhi at 213 for six. Dev Lakra (13) and Hrithik Shokeen (8) fell soon after, while Divij Mehra scored 21 off 28 balls to help Delhi move closer to the 277-run mark. Navdeep Saini remained unbeaten on 20.Pramanik was Bengal's leading wicket-taker with three wickets, while Gani and Gupta took two each. Mohammed Shami, Akash Deep and Mukesh Kumar claimed one wicket apiece.In the chase, Ankur Paul scored 38 off 41 balls, including two fours and a six, before losing his wicket. Captain Easwaran remained unbeaten on 34 off 40 balls, while Sudip Gharami, who had scored a century in the first innings, finished on 16 not out off 12 deliveries as Bengal reached the target without further trouble.Desai's fifer guides Gujarat to 10-wicket win over OdishaIn Ahmedabad, left-arm spinner Siddharth Desai took five wickets to help Gujarat beat Odisha by 10 wickets in their Group C match. The win also earned Gujarat a bonus point as they began their campaign under new-season coach Monty Desai.Odisha resumed the day at 119 for four but were bowled out for 161 in 46.1 overs, with Siddharth Desai taking 5/36. Gujarat needed just 47 runs to win and completed the chase without losing a wicket in 9.3 overs.Sandeep Pattnaik top-scored for Odisha with 65, while Ninad Rathva made 53. Odisha lost seven wickets in their second innings as Desai led the collapse to claim his 16th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket.Left-arm pacer Arzan Nagwaswalla also played a key role for Gujarat, finishing with six wickets in the match, including 3/33 in the second innings.The Group C match between Jharkhand and Kerala in Jamshedpur ended in a draw, with the hosts earning three points after taking a first-innings lead. articles.title: 'Singlebloodymindedness': Shukri Conrad's fiery wake-up call after South Africa's 214-run defeat to Australia
articles.summary: South Africa head coach Shukri Conrad wants his batters to develop a combination of intense focus and stubborn resistance after their 214-run defeat to
articles.body: South Africa head coach Shukri Conrad wants his batters to develop a combination of intense focus and stubborn resistance after their 214-run defeat to Australia in the first Test at Kingsmead. Frustrated by a series of poor shot selections that contributed to the hosts' collapse, Conrad coined the term “singlebloodymindedness” to underline the attitude required to survive against a world-class bowling attack.While Aiden Markram offered a lesson in patience with a determined second-innings knock of 75, Conrad believes the rest of the batting unit must learn to dig deeper when the pressure mounts. For the South African coach, the defeat was not merely about technical shortcomings but also about the mental discipline needed to succeed in Test cricket.“Aiden showed us in the second innings that there’s nothing fancy about Test cricket,” Conrad told reporters after the match on Tuesday. “It’s that singlebloodymindedness- ‘I’ve got to bat for a day-and-a-half, irrespective of what it looks like’. Some of our batters can take a leaf out of his book.”Markram's patience offers South Africa a blueprintMarkram stood out in South Africa's attempt to save the Test, spending just under six hours at the crease and facing 237 deliveries for his 75 runs. His innings was comfortably the longest stay by a South African batter during the fourth-innings effort.Wiaan Mulder provided the next-best resistance, batting for more than two hours, while David Bedingham was the only other batter to spend more than an hour at the crease. Only Markram and Mulder faced more than 100 deliveries, highlighting the lack of sustained resistance from the rest of the batting order.South Africa's problems had intensified on the third day when they lost Markram, Temba Bavuma and Bedingham within 9.3 overs, adding just 15 runs during that collapse. Their final six wickets then fell for 129 runs, leaving the hosts unable to mount a serious challenge. The manner of the dismissals particularly concerned Conrad, who felt several batters were undone by their decision-making rather than simply by Australia's bowling quality.'A lot of our dismissals sat in the mental corner'Asked whether the poor shot selection had left him and batting coach Ashwell Prince frustrated, Conrad responded with a joke about their shaved heads before acknowledging the seriousness of the problem.“There's a singlemindedness that goes with Test batting, especially against a world-class attack like Australia's,” he said.The South African coach admitted that the team's shot selection had been frustrating but stopped short of placing the blame on individual players.“Where do you apportion blame? Do you apportion blame? We need to be better after this. Yes, we were pulling the last strands [of hair] out with some of the decision-making and the shot-making,” Conrad said.He categorised dismissals into three areas: technical, tactical and mental and suggested that the mental aspect had played a significant role in South Africa's batting struggles.“Dismissals sit in one of three places; technical, tactical or mental. A lot of our dismissals sat in the mental corner. Is that an easier fix than technical and tactical?
